title: Paloma and the Visitor
premise: Ada Galloway hosts a small-town overnight radio show, until callers begin phoning in — people she knows died the week before. When her childhood imaginary friend, Paloma, appears on her porch unchanged after twenty years, Ada learns the town's founders bound something beneath the radio tower, and every generation must renew the ritual or the dead come home wrong. Pulled into the middle of it by Paloma, who is not a friend but a warden wearing a friendly shape, Ada must choose between finishing the founders' ritual — which requires a living heir to stay behind forever — and breaking it, knowing the thing below will walk free. In the end Ada rewrites the ritual itself, offering the broadcast instead of a body: her voice, transmitted endlessly into the dark, sealing the door while keeping herself alive but never again alone.
about_author: Ines Eriksen is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer from coastal Maine who spent years collecting listeners' stories of grief and things that go unanswered. Their fiction blends small-town intimacy with slow-burning dread.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Ada. During her overnight show, a caller describes his own funeral in detail; Ada checks the obituaries and confirms he died Tuesday. She keeps broadcasting, voice steady, hands shaking. Beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada reveals her compulsions: counting doors, keeping lights on, rituals inherited from her grandmother. A second dead caller asks her to 'tell them we're coming back.' Beat: isolation deepening; the reader learns Ada has always half-believed.

chapters.title: Paloma on the Porch
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At dawn, an unchanged child figure waits on her porch — Paloma, her imaginary friend at age seven, now impossibly real and exactly as remembered. Paloma says only: 'It's time you came home.' Beat: uncanny warmth that curdles.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada returns to her hometown, Hollow Creek, where the radio tower stands over a sealed well. Old neighbors greet her with rehearsed kindness; none will meet her eyes. Beat: belonging offered like a trap.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ada, with flashbacks in her grandmother's voice via old cassette tapes. The ledger lists names of 'keepers' across generations — Galloways always last. Each name is paired with a date and the word 'renewed.' Beat: inheritance as sentence.

chapters.title: Wrong Frequencies
chapters.summary: POV Marcus, the station engineer. He shows Ada recordings of static that resolves into voices when played backward — including her grandmother's. The tower isn't broadcasting out; it's holding something in. Beat: the machinery of horror revealed.

chapters.title: What the Dead Want
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Dead callers converge physically: they stand at the edge of her headlights, polite, patient, asking to be let through the counted doors. Paloma drives them off with a sound like a struck bell. Beat: terror tempered by protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Partially Read
chapters.summary: POV Ada. In the founder's house, Ada reads the rite: it requires blood of the line spoken into the tower at the turning of the season — three nights away. The final page is torn out. Beat: agency within constraint.

chapters.title: Paloma Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada confronts Paloma about what she really is. Paloma answers only in Ada's own childhood words, mirroring her — a warden shaped by memory, bound to the same duty. Beat: grief for a friendship that was never real.

chapters.title: The Congregation
chapters.summary: POV Reverend Hale, descendant of the founders. He gathers the town, revealing they all know; they've always known, and the Galloways have always paid. He offers Ada welcome — as sacrifice. Beat: power's corruption made communal.

chapters.title: Doors, Counted
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The dead begin entering houses despite locked doors; Ada realizes her counting has been holding thresholds shut all along — her compulsions were inherited wards. One door fails. Beat: guilt weaponized.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: POV Marcus. Marcus finds the missing ledger page hidden in the tower's base: the ritual doesn't seal the thing below — it feeds it, and the founders built the town as a farm. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Night Call-In
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada broadcasts openly about the truth; the switchboard floods with the dead telling their versions — some begging for release, some warning her the thing below wears voices too. Beat: moral complexity; not all dead are innocent.

chapters.title: Paloma's First Lie
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Paloma admits she has guided every Galloway heir to the tower for two hundred years — and that she loves Ada, which changes nothing about her purpose. Beat: betrayal braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Turning Season
chapters.summary: POV multiple, interwoven. The eve of the ritual: fog rises from the well, the town seals itself in, Hale leads hymns, and the dead stand in every yard waiting for midnight. Beat: held breath before climax.

chapters.title: Into the Tower
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Hale and the congregation escort Ada up the tower stairs; Paloma walks beside her, hand in hers like when she was seven. At the top, the microphone waits over the open well-mouth. Beat: sacrificial calm.

chapters.title: The Voice Below
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The thing beneath speaks in her grandmother's voice, then her mother's, then her own — offering her the torn page's alternative: rule beside it instead of feeding it. Power, freely given. Beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: What Ada Refuses
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada rejects both options — the founders' feeding and the entity's bargain — and begins improvising: she opens the broadcast, giving the dead callers the airtime they've begged for, letting them speak themselves out. Beat: defiance as creativity.

chapters.title: Every Voice at Once
chapters.summary: POV Marcus at the board, Ada at the mic. The dead pour their unfinished words through the signal; the entity, starved of silence and secrets, recoils. Paloma holds the threshold open, burning down to outline. Beat: climax — communion as weapon.

chapters.title: The New Ritual
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada speaks the closing words she wrote herself: her voice, ongoing, becomes the seal — the tower now transmits her show eternally into the dark, a lighthouse of speech. The well closes. Hale's congregation scatters, stripped of purpose. Beat: cost and triumph entangled.

chapters.title: After the Sign-Off
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Weeks later: the dead are gone, the town hollowed but honest, Marcus running the transmitter that carries Ada's endless broadcast. Her compulsions quiet; the doors stay uncounted. Beat: exhausted peace.

chapters.title: Paloma, Unchanged
chapters.summary: POV Ada. On the porch one last dawn, Paloma appears — freed now, or perhaps simply finished — and asks if Ada still wants a friend. Ada says yes, this time knowing exactly what she's choosing. Final line: the light stays on, and someone stays with it. Beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
